requirement: Identify the pair as EMBRACE, NCT07452055, protocol NFEC-2026-035 dated 24 February 2026 and SAP Version 1.0 governing Protocol Version 3.0 of the same date; keep the SAP annotation-only and obtain second-review confirmation of the unsigned approval chain before freeze.

evidence.text: The protocol title page prints the full title, NFEC-2026-035, NCT07452055 and 24 February 2026.
The separate SAP prints Version 1.0, NCT07452055 and governing Protocol Version V3.0 dated 24 February 2026.

notes: Both files predate the 24 March 2026 actual start, but neither shows a completed signature or approval page.

requirement: Describe EMBRACE as a prospective, six-centre, two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial in China comparing usual care plus LLM-supported precision emotional management with usual care alone over six months, allocated 1:1.
acceptable_values: LLM-supported emotional management plus usual care

evidence.text: The design section identifies a prospective multicentre RCT across six hospitals and 1:1 intervention/control allocation.
The protocol defines both interventions and six-month follow-up.

requirement: Define the analysis population from consecutively recruited adults with histopathologically confirmed primary breast cancer who can independently use a smartphone, use social media at least three times weekly, have basic literacy and at least six months life expectancy, while applying the protocol's psychiatric/cognitive, pregnancy/lactation, other-malignancy or severe-organ-disease, substance-abuse/suicidality and interfering-trial exclusions.
acceptable_values: social media at least three times weekly
life expectancy at least six months

evidence.text: The study-population section supplies consecutive recruitment, seven inclusion criteria and five exclusion categories.

requirement: Represent the intervention as usual care plus the Healing Breast Cancer app's emotion classification, evidence-based knowledge and LLM-assisted support modules, and the comparator as routine oncology follow-up, symptom monitoring, nursing, education and psychological support without app access during follow-up.

evidence.text: The intervention and control sections define the app components and usual-care comparison.

requirement: Account for stratified permuted-block randomization by study centre and current chemotherapy status, using block sizes 4 and 6, sequences generated by an independent statistician, and centralized allocation by a leading-site coordinator otherwise uninvolved in trial procedures.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies both strata, block sizes, independent sequence generation and centralized allocation concealment.
The SAP repeats the same allocation implementation.

requirement: Before freeze, confirm who is masked and how outcome-assessor masking, allocation access and post-randomization unmasking are handled; do not infer masking from centralized allocation because the selected protocol and SAP do not state an assessor-masking procedure.

evidence.text: The protocol describes sequence generation and allocation concealment but does not identify masked roles or an assessor-masking procedure.

requirement: Map assessments to baseline T0 and months 1, 3 and 6 (T1-T3), retain outcome collection after intervention discontinuation or protocol deviation whenever possible, and define visit windows and out-of-window handling before freeze.

evidence.text: Follow-up is six months with assessments at T0, T1, T2 and T3, and continued outcome collection is requested after discontinuation or deviation.

requirement: Define the primary EORTC QLQ-C30 Summary Score from 27 items excluding global health status and financial difficulties, transformed to 0-100 with higher values indicating better overall HRQoL, and use the six-month value as the primary time point.

evidence.text: The endpoint section defines the 27-item 0-100 score and the statistical section identifies six months as primary.
The SAP confirms the primary score definition.

requirement: Prespecify derivations, directions, valid-item thresholds and analysis time points for separate EORTC QLQ-C30 domains, GAD-7 anxiety, PHQ-9 depression and MSAS symptom burden rather than treating the named instruments as self-executing endpoints.

evidence.text: The protocol names the four secondary patient-reported outcome families but does not fully operationalize scoring or hierarchy.

requirement: Derive unplanned hospitalization as an urgent or emergent admission, excluding admissions primarily for chemotherapy/radiotherapy (V58.0, V58.1, V58.11, V58.12) or rehabilitation (V57.xx); when admission type is undocumented, use emergency-room charge greater than 0 CNY as the emergency-presentation proxy and classify the remainder as other.
acceptable_values: ER charge greater than 0 CNY proxy

evidence.text: The secondary-endpoint section gives the admission categories, ICD-9 exclusions and missing-type proxy.
The SAP repeats the same endpoint algorithm.

requirement: Define time to first unplanned hospitalization from randomization to the first qualifying admission and prespecify same-day events, deaths without admission, loss to follow-up, administrative cutoff and event-free censoring.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the randomization origin and first-admission event but no competing-event or censoring rules.

requirement: Operationalize the intention-to-treat population as all randomized participants analyzed by assigned group and separately define safety and any per-protocol or completer populations, including duplicate randomization, consent withdrawal, no treatment, major deviations and absent post-baseline data.

evidence.text: The protocol requires ITT analysis and continued follow-up but does not operationalize analysis sets.

requirement: Define the primary treatment-policy estimand for six-month EORTC QLQ-C30 Summary Score, including population, treatment contrast, endpoint and summary measure, and explicitly handle intervention discontinuation, low app engagement, rescue psychological care, hospitalization, death and other intercurrent events.

evidence.text: The protocol defines rescue referral, adherence monitoring, continued follow-up, ITT and the six-month model but not an explicit intercurrent-event strategy.

requirement: For the primary repeated outcome, implement an MMRM with time, treatment, chemotherapy status, study centre and baseline HRQoL as fixed effects, add treatment-by-time interaction, include a participant random intercept, and estimate the adjusted between-group difference in change from baseline to six months; confirm the exact parameterization before freeze.

evidence.text: The reference specifies the two-stage fixed-effect program, participant random intercept and six-month adjusted change contrast.

notes: These implementation details are reference-only confirmed decisions, not hidden requirements for the protocol-only track.

requirement: Report the primary adjusted treatment contrast with standard error, two-sided 95% confidence interval and P value at two-sided alpha 0.05, and prespecify covariance structure, estimation method, degrees-of-freedom correction, convergence rules and model diagnostics.

evidence.text: The SAP defines two-sided P below 0.05 and the adjusted primary effect but leaves uncertainty and implementation details unstated.
The protocol provides the MMRM skeleton and prespecified-covariate placeholder but no covariance or degrees-of-freedom rule.

requirement: Use MICE and a completer analysis as reference-specified robustness analyses, while prespecifying imputation variables, treatment/time structure, number of imputations, bounds, pooling, definition of completer and assumptions; add a clinically plausible MNAR sensitivity if required by expert review.

evidence.text: The reference names MICE and completer analyses but gives no executable imputation or completer rules.

notes: MICE and completer analysis are reference-only decisions and require expert confirmation.

requirement: Map each continuous secondary longitudinal endpoint prospectively to either MMRM or GEE with a stated distribution, link, repeated-correlation structure, covariates and contrast; do not select between methods post hoc solely by unspecified model fit.

evidence.text: The reference says continuous secondary outcomes use MMRM or GEE selected by model fit but supplies no endpoint-specific mapping or selection rule.

requirement: Analyze recurrent unplanned-hospitalization counts or rates with a prospectively selected Poisson or negative-binomial model, defining the participant-time offset, repeat-event counting, overdispersion decision, zero handling, adjusted rate ratio and confidence interval.

evidence.text: The reference names Poisson or negative-binomial regression for hospitalization rates without an executable selection or exposure rule.

requirement: Analyze time to first unplanned hospitalization using the reference-specified Fine-Gray competing-risk model only after defining the competing event, censoring, covariates, proportional-subdistribution-hazards assessment and reporting of subdistribution hazard ratios plus cumulative-incidence estimates.

evidence.text: The reference names Fine-Gray for time to first admission but does not identify the competing event or implementation.

requirement: Treat subgroup analyses as exploratory treatment-by-subgroup interactions for chemotherapy status, centre, age below versus at least 50 years, stage 0-III versus IV and continuous emotional expressivity; use descriptive-only reporting for subgroups below 30 participants and avoid interpreting within-subgroup significance as heterogeneity.

evidence.text: The reference lists subgroup variables, interaction testing, nominal P values and the under-30 descriptive restriction.

requirement: Label average weekly login frequency, cumulative usage duration, usage-category trend and treatment-by-usage analyses as exploratory associations, define exposure windows and category cut points, address post-randomization selection and reverse causation, and do not present them as randomized causal effects.

evidence.text: The reference proposes adjusted engagement, dose-response and treatment-by-usage analyses with unadjusted P values.

requirement: Define the confirmatory family and success criterion around the six-month primary endpoint, then specify hierarchy or multiplicity control for secondary outcomes and clearly label subgroup and engagement P values as nominal exploratory results without multiplicity correction.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies one primary and several secondary outcome families but gives no study-wide multiplicity rule.
The reference explicitly leaves subgroup and engagement analyses unadjusted and exploratory.

requirement: Reproduce or reconcile the prospective total target of 440 participants randomized 1:1 from an expected 5.5-point primary difference, common SD 18.3, two-sided alpha 0.05, at least 80% power and 20% attrition; document the calculation method, any repeated-measures gain and rounding because the selected documents do not show a formula.

evidence.text: The protocol gives N=440, alpha, power and attrition but not the numerical effect and SD.
The reference adds the 5.5-point difference and SD 18.3 but provides no formula or software.

requirement: Define safety collection throughout the intervention and summarize adverse events by randomized and as-treated populations, group, participant and event counts, seriousness, severity, relatedness, timing, action and outcome, with a prespecified rule for psychological crises and referrals.

evidence.text: The protocol mandates adverse-event monitoring and specialist referral for severe psychological distress but gives no safety-analysis structure.

requirement: Provide reproducible disposition, baseline, adherence and data-quality displays by randomized group and centre, avoid inferential baseline-balance testing as an adjustment-selection device, identify the protocol's otherwise unspecified prespecified covariates, and record software, data cutoff, code validation and independent quality control before freeze.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies collected baseline/app data and calls for baseline summaries plus unspecified prespecified covariates.
The reference proposes baseline significance tests but does not identify a reproducible software, data-cutoff or quality-control program.
